rationale: Seventh investigation, taking up the lead the window scenario raised: the lease's coherence with the leader's own contact refresh interval. The map now carries the leadership fact (the node holds the leadership of a term until it leaves it, whether by traffic from another leader, by its own lease check or by a higher term) and the obligation c-reachable-quorum-keeps-leadership states that a leader must not leave the leadership while it can contact a quorum. The check uses the exploration harness but sharpens the witness: every node's intervals are lengthened through the library's own reload API so no peer campaigns, an observer records the leader's first departure from the leadership together with the term it held then and its peers' states and terms at that instant, and a probe afterwards shows a quorum answering in the same term.

candidate.rationale: Seventh Candidate, opened from the lease lead the window scenario recorded. It states the duty that a leader keeps its leadership while a quorum is reachable and binds it to the lease check that decides it.

b-elect-self.preserves: The behavior's owner, trigger, guards, reads, writes, branches, asynchronous boundaries, protections and its existing produced and consumed facts are unchanged; only an additional produced fact is declared.

b-client-apply-verify.preserves: The behavior's owner, trigger, guards, branches, asynchronous boundaries, protections and its existing consumed facts are unchanged; only an additional consumed fact is declared, so the client-contract obligations keep their basis.

question.question: Can a node that holds the leadership of a term leave it while a quorum of the voters of its configuration is reachable and no higher term exists, when the configuration it runs was accepted by the library itself, including through its reload API?
question.importance: A leader that leaves the leadership for a reason the lease was not meant to detect causes an unnecessary election and, if the peers' own timeouts are long, a leadership gap during which no writes commit. The lease check exists to detect lost connectivity, so a step-down that happens with a fully reachable quorum means the mechanism is reporting a condition that does not hold; and because the relation between the lease and the interval at which a leader refreshes contact is not part of the accepted configurations' validation, an operator can reach this state through the library's own APIs without any error. The consequence is bounded - the cluster re-elects - but the trigger is the library's own accepted configuration rather than a fault.
contexts: three connected voters with no partition, a lease fixed at five seconds and intervals lengthened through the library's reload API after the election
the leader's own lease check firing while both peers answer in the leader's term
event_paths: leader path: the lease timer fires, contacted counts the local server and any peer whose last contact is within the lease, and a contacted count below the quorum transitions the node to follower
peer path: both peers stay followers in the same term because their own intervals were lengthened, so no higher term appears
observation: the leader's first departure from the leadership is recorded with its term and the peers' states and terms at that instant, and a probe afterwards answers in the same term

supporting_behavior_ids.b-client-apply-verify: the client contract reports the leadership claim the lease can end
supporting_behavior_ids.b-term-observation: shows that leaving the leadership does not by itself change the term, which is why the recorded term is the discriminator

counterevidence: The library's own defaults keep the relation coherent (heartbeat timeout one second, lease five hundred milliseconds), so this behaviour requires a deliberate interval choice.

The lease is documented as a staleness bound rather than a connectivity probe, so a leader that has not heard from a quorum recently is meant to step down; the question is only whether an interval relation the library accepts can make that unavoidable with a reachable quorum.
The peers' own timeouts determine how long the cluster stays leaderless, so the observed consequence is an unnecessary election in this prefix rather than a long gap.
The lease check counts the leader itself, so a two voter cluster behaves differently from the three voter cluster used here.
unknowns: whether ValidateConfig, the reload path or the lease check is the intended place to enforce the relation
how wide the interval relation must be before the step-down is certain rather than likely
whether the same relation can be broken through the initial configuration alone
question.trigger_rationale: checkLeaderLease counts a voter as contacted only when the time since its last contact is within LeaderLeaseTimeout, while a leader's contact with a reachable peer is refreshed at an interval derived from HeartbeatTimeout together with the replication loop's CommitTimeout. The lease is fixed at creation and ReloadConfig validates only that it does not exceed the heartbeat timeout, so lengthening the heartbeat interval at runtime moves a coherent relation into an incoherent one; with a lease of five seconds and a heartbeat interval of three hundred seconds the leader cannot satisfy its own check and leaves the leadership with both peers reachable and in its own term.

obligation.description: A node that holds the leadership of a term must not leave it while a quorum of the voters of the current configuration is reachable and no higher term exists. The requirement binds the lease check and the configuration the library accepts together: the check exists to detect lost connectivity, so a configuration the library validates, including one applied through its reload API, must not make the check unsatisfiable with a reachable quorum.

scope.description: A cluster of voters in the captured module whose lease timeout and heartbeat timeout are within the range ValidateConfig accepts, including changes applied at runtime through ReloadConfig.
assumptions: the peers are reachable and in the leader's term
the lease timeout is fixed for the node's lifetime, as the captured implementation provides no reloadable lease
excluded: the obligations already checked (term publication, client-future completion, the vote rule, the two-leader overlap, the configuration index and the committed-entry rule)
partitions and unreachable peers, which the lease is meant to detect
behaviour of callers or transports outside the module

pending: which layer should enforce the relation between the lease and the contact refresh interval
how the relation behaves at its boundary

grounding.derivation: checkLeaderLease measures the elapsed time since each voter's last contact against LeaderLeaseTimeout and steps the leader down when fewer than a quorum have been contacted, counting the local server itself; its own comment states the step-down means the leader may have lost connectivity (s-raft-leader-lease). The contact a leader has with a reachable peer is refreshed by the replication loop and by a heartbeat goroutine whose interval derives from HeartbeatTimeout (s-replication-heartbeat, s-raft-set-current-term), while the lease is set once and ReloadConfig changes only the reloadable intervals and validates only that the lease does not exceed the heartbeat timeout. The requirement therefore holds that no accepted configuration may make the check unsatisfiable while a quorum is reachable.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any configuration the library accepts, including one applied at runtime; the check exercises a three voter cluster with a five second lease and intervals lengthened to three hundred seconds.
unresolved: whether the initial configuration alone can break it
alternatives: the combination could be treated as the operator's responsibility, since the library's defaults are coherent and the documentation warns that the lease must be a fraction of the heartbeat timeout
the lease check could be changed to distinguish 'no recent contact' from 'no contact at all'

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the requirement's negation: it ends the leadership on a staleness measure whose refresh cadence another configuration field controls, so an accepted configuration can make it end a leadership while a quorum is reachable.

bindings.description: Raft.checkLeaderLease counts the voters whose last contact is within LeaderLeaseTimeout, including the local server, and transitions the node to follower when that count is below the quorum; it is the rule that decides whether the leadership claim survives.
pending: whether the repair belongs here, in the accepted configuration, or in the reload path
